extra_misconceptions.fact: Prevention stops an event from occurring, while mitigation reduces the severity of damage from events that cannot be prevented.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mitigation and prevention are identical phases that both eliminate an emergency before it begins.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Recovery planning starts alongside active response so utilities, shelter, and community services can be restored without delay.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Recovery work only begins after every emergency responder has completely left the disaster scene.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Natural weather and seismic events cannot be prevented, so preparedness focuses on mitigation, warning systems, and protection.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Natural hazards like earthquakes or hurricanes can be stopped through neighborhood prevention programs.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A complete preparedness matrix must document specific actions for prevention, protection, mitigation, response, and recovery.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A preparedness chart only needs to list immediate first-aid steps taken during the crisis itself.

extra_socratic_questions: What sequence of actions shifts an active emergency response into long-term community recovery?
Which operational goal separates pre-incident hazard mitigation from active crisis protection?
What specific details belong in your requirement 1b matrix to track each hazard across all five phases?
Why is it dangerous to wait until the response phase to test backup power and warning radios?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Local cellular voice networks often overload during disasters, so families should text or call an out-of-town contact instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Local family members should call each other directly on cell phones immediately after a major disaster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Airborne chemical spills, tornadoes, and severe winter storms often require sheltering in an interior room rather than driving.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Evacuating the neighborhood is always safer than staying inside your house during any emergency.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Families need both a spot right outside the home for fires and a second location outside the neighborhood if roads are closed.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: One meeting spot at the end of the driveway is enough for a complete family evacuation plan.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only shut off the main gas valve if you smell gas or hear a leak, because a utility technician must restore service afterward.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Shutting off the main natural gas valve should be part of every routine family evacuation drill.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should your family establish its two meeting points in case home roads are blocked?
Under what hazard conditions should a household shelter in place rather than evacuate immediately?
What contact numbers and medical details must be recorded on every family member's wallet card?
Which physical indicator confirms that a home room is properly sealed against outside airborne hazards?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The test button only checks battery power and horn circuitry, so alarms must also be vacuumed and replaced every ten years.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pressing the test button on a smoke alarm verifies that its internal smoke chamber is clean and clear.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High-wattage space heaters can overheat power strip wiring and cause fires, so they must plug directly into wall receptacles.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Power strips with built-in circuit breakers allow you to safely plug multiple space heaters into one outlet.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dry chemical extinguishers can lose pressure or cake over time, requiring monthly gauge checks and periodic maintenance.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An ABC fire extinguisher stays ready for use forever as long as the safety pin remains in place.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Foot traffic crushes wire insulation under rugs and traps heat, creating a hidden ignition source for house fires.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Extension cords run underneath hallway rugs are safe because the carpet protects the wire from wear.

extra_socratic_questions: What inspection sequence ensures you check electrical, fire, and fall hazards across every level?
What sensor mechanism distinguishes a photoelectric smoke alarm from a carbon monoxide detector?
What measurement confirms that a home water heater thermostat is set low enough to prevent scalds?
Why is it dangerous to store gasoline or paint thinner inside a utility closet near a pilot light?

extra_misconceptions.fact: High-voltage outdoor lines can arc through wood, so non-conductive tool rescues apply only to low-voltage household wiring.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A dry wooden broomstick can safely push any fallen outdoor utility power line off an injured victim.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cloth masks cannot filter carbon monoxide and holding your breath fails under exertion, so ventilate and call 911 first.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Holding your breath or wearing a dust mask protects you while rescuing someone from carbon monoxide.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standing concentrates weight on thin ice and causes it to break, so rescuers must lie flat and reach with a pole or rope.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Walking upright to the edge of an ice hole lets you pull a submerged victim out with maximum leverage.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Running fans the flames and accelerates severe burns; victims must immediately stop, drop to the ground, and roll to smother fire.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Running toward a water source is the fastest way to extinguish clothing that has caught on fire.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout position their body on shore or ice before extending a pole to a victim?
Under what condition does an energized power line require utility crews instead of a wooden broom rescue?
Which physical symptom or alarm reading alerts you that a building contains lethal carbon monoxide?
Why is it dangerous to hold a wet cloth over your nose and enter a basement filled with carbon monoxide?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The human voice fatigues quickly and fades in wind, whereas a survival whistle carries over a mile with minimal energy.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Shouting for help carries farther through dense forest than blowing a pea-less plastic survival whistle.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cold water saps strength and causes hypothermia rapidly, while a floating hull provides buoyancy and a large target for searchers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Swimming toward a distant shoreline is safer than staying next to an overturned canoe in cold water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A dedicated signal mirror includes a retro-reflective aiming hole that lets you place the flash directly onto distant aircraft.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any ordinary flat bathroom mirror works just as accurately at long range as a sighting signal mirror.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thick white smoke from green foliage is only visible by day, whereas bright dry-wood flames are required for night signaling.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding green leaves to a signal fire at night produces the most visible distress beacon for aircraft.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should you aim the reflected beam of a signal mirror relative to a distant rescue aircraft?
What visual pattern distinguishes an international ground-to-air distress symbol from normal camp gear?
What cadence and blast count confirm that a whistle signal is a universal call for emergency help?
Why is it dangerous to swim away from a capsized boat toward shore instead of signaling from the hull?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Turning sleeves inside out inside the zipped jackets prevents the zippers from splitting open and keeps the poles from spreading.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pulling jacket sleeves right-side out outside the poles keeps the fabric tighter on a jacket stretcher.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Every improvised stretcher must be tested by lifting an uninjured Scout of similar weight first to verify pole and knot strength.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Lifting an injured patient onto a new improvised litter immediately saves valuable rescue time.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Patients are normally carried feet-first so the rear bearer can watch their face and prevent blood from pooling in the head.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Carrying a stretcher patient head-first down a steep trail is always the safest transport orientation.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dead branches on the ground are often brittle with rot and can snap under load, so only strong hardwood poles or staves work.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Green deadwood branches gathered from the forest floor make reliable poles for a wilderness litter.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should you position jacket sleeves when building a two-pole improvised stretcher for a patient?
Under what spinal injury suspicion must rescuers immobilize a victim rather than use a blanket drag?
What load test confirms that an improvised rope or blanket litter will not collapse under a patient?
Why is it dangerous for stretcher bearers to walk in step when carrying a victim over rough terrain?

extra_misconceptions.fact: ICS is a modular, scalable management system used every day for incidents as small as a single-car crash or local search.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The Incident Command System is only activated for massive federal disasters involving multiple states.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Self-dispatching without checking in at the staging area violates ICS accountability and puts unbriefed responders at risk.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Trained volunteers who arrive at a disaster scene should immediately begin searching damaged buildings.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ten-codes vary across agencies and cause dangerous confusion, so NIMS requires plain-language communication on all channels.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Police ten-codes speed up emergency radio communication when fire, medical, and Scout units work together.

extra_misconceptions.fact: ICS expands and contracts as needed, and the Incident Commander performs all functions not explicitly delegated to a chief.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every ICS section chief must be appointed even when managing a small neighborhood emergency event.

extra_socratic_questions: What check-in procedure must a volunteer unit follow upon arriving at an active Incident Command Post?
Which organizational role separates the National Incident Management System from local ICS operations?
What span-of-control ratio confirms that an ICS supervisor is not managing too many subordinates?
Why is it dangerous to use agency-specific ten-codes on multi-jurisdictional disaster radio channels?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouts must never direct motor vehicle traffic on active streets and are restricted to guiding pedestrians in safe areas.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scouts in full uniform are authorized to stand in active roadways and direct vehicle traffic during storms.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Spoken messages easily become distorted under stress, so Scout messengers must carry written dispatches with time and sender logs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Delivering emergency messages verbally from memory is faster and more reliable than carrying written notes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Youth protection and emergency safety rules strictly require Scouts to travel in buddy pairs or teams with adult supervision.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A fast older Scout can run emergency messenger routes alone at night to cover twice as much ground.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mobilization kits must be packed, inspected, and kept ready in advance so a Scout can depart immediately when called.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A personal emergency service pack can be assembled quickly from household closets after an alert sounds.

extra_socratic_questions: What phone-tree sequence enables a Scout troop to mobilize all patrols when cell towers fail?
Which safety boundary separates youth Scout crowd-control duties from adult law enforcement traffic stops?
What timestamps and routing details must a Scout messenger record on every written dispatch slip?
Which reflective gear and buddy-system rules must be verified before Scouts deploy on messenger routes?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Releasing a tourniquet in the field restarts lethal arterial hemorrhage; only a physician or paramedic should loosen it.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Loosening an applied extremity tourniquet every fifteen minutes prevents tissue necrosis while waiting for paramedics.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Responders must first verify scene safety, check responsiveness, and confirm the absence of normal breathing before compressions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation should begin immediately on every unconscious victim found during a multi-casualty disaster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Perishable sterile dressings expire and psychomotor skills fade, requiring routine kit audits and regular hands-on practice.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Earning the First Aid merit badge once guarantees lifelong competency without inspecting kit supplies or refreshing skills.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pulling out an impaled object unplugs damaged blood vessels; stabilize the object in place with bulky dressings instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Removing an impaled shard of glass from a deep wound allows firmer direct pressure to stop severe bleeding.

extra_socratic_questions: What sequence of life-threat checks must a responder complete before splinting a victim's fractured forearm at a disaster site?
Which physical indicator distinguishes life-threatening heatstroke from heat exhaustion during a summer mobilization?
What measurement confirms that a windlass tourniquet is tight enough, and where must the exact application time be recorded?
Why is it dangerous to begin treating a bleeding disaster victim before putting on nitrile gloves and checking scene hazards?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Disaster managers spend most of their year on hazard mitigation, interagency drills, grant administration, and public training.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Emergency services coordinators work only when hurricanes, wildfires, or floods actively strike their local jurisdiction.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Field incident commanders direct tactical crews, while emergency coordinators manage multi-agency logistics and policy in the EOC.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: County emergency management directors personally command front-line fire hoses and tactical rescue rigs at every incident.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many pathways begin with FEMA Independent Study courses, volunteer CERT service, or technical Emergency Medical Technician training.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Disaster management careers require a four-year university degree before a candidate can earn any emergency credentials.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most emergency management civil servants work at municipal, county, tribal, or state agencies where local disasters first unfold.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Civil servants in disaster management work exclusively for the federal government inside Washington headquarters offices.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to municipal resource requests when a local emergency manager activates an Emergency Operations Center?
Under what condition does a civil service disaster coordinator transition from mitigation planning to active incident support?
What specific FEMA Incident Command System certifications should you log when comparing three disaster management career paths?
Where should a Scout verify a public official's agency role and emergency duty schedule before conducting a career interview?
